Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training

test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

SASRec encodes interaction sequences with item embeddings, learned positional embeddings, and causal self-attention blocks. Each position predicts the next item through a dot product with shared item embeddings. Attention lets predictions draw on recent actions or longer histories.  ## Search results
Recent work supports separating semantic similarity from complementary compatibility. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complements as relevant yet dissimilar, combining low-pass and mid-pass graph filters with attention. [MMSC (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22268) separates behavioral and semantic representations for substitute/complement inference, but uses foundation models and LLM-generated augmentation, outside this task’s restrictions. [AlleCompanion (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063) emphasizes that co-purchases are noisy evidence of compatibility; its category constraints, expert rules and LLM reasoning also require unavailable inputs.

For sequential prediction, [GaGNN (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2024.120623) combines group and individual transition graphs with sequential encoding. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) adds textual item representations to a SASRec-derived model, but relies on BERT and reviews; it does not establish effectiveness for a lightweight encoder trained from scratch using only titles/descriptions. These papers provide architectural motivation, rather than a directly compliant recipe.

A task-compatible hypothesis: retain SASRec, add separate directed-transition and text-similarity branches, and learn their fusion through next-item supervision. Encode titles/descriptions with randomly initialized token embeddings and mean pooling or a small CNN; construct graph edges exclusively from training histories. Treat branches as predictive signals, not verified complement/substitute labels: consecutive interactions alone cannot establish either relation, especially for movies and music. Compare ID-only, graph-only, text-only and fused variants using the pinned macro validation HR@10; improvements under that protocol remain unverified.

---

Recent work supports separating interests across temporal scales. **MSMT-LSI (2024)** combines multihead attention with long- and short-term temporal embeddings; **IBLSRec (2025)** distinguishes stable item relationships from transient interactions and uses inferred intent to refine preferences, explicitly targeting sparsity. **MIMAR-SRec (AAAI 2026)** models intent across contextual windows, aligns representations with intent prototypes, and adds robustness to interaction and temporal noise. These papers treat intent as learned from behavior, rather than observed psychological traits. Sources: [MSMT-LSI](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5), [IBLSRec](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10820829/), [MIMAR-SRec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489).

Mixture-of-experts offers complementary mechanisms. **HyMoERec (2025 preprint; AAAI 2026 student abstract)** combines a shared dense expert with sparse specialized experts and learnable fusion. **Mixture of Sequence (WWW 2026)** routes histories into latent themes and combines global, short-term, and theme-specific experts. **TriSSR (2026)** adaptively fuses sequence, frequency-scale, and temporal-interval experts. A practical inference for this benchmark: retain SASRec as the recent-context branch, add masked full-history pooling and a small latent-intent expert bank, then learn a gate conditioned on context, history length, and available time gaps. Sparse-history benefits remain a hypothesis; compare against simpler two-branch fusion using the common macro validation HR@10, and inspect gate saturation and expert utilization. Sources: [HyMoERec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06388), [Mixture of Sequence](https://q-rz.github.io/static/www26/www26-mos-paper.pdf), [TriSSR](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925231226009707).

---

Recent evidence supports testing stronger multi-negative objectives. [gSASRec’s IJCAI 2024 summary](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec weaknesses partly to overconfidence under sampled BCE; its authors recommend 128–256 negatives with generalized BCE, balancing accuracy and cost. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies sampled softmax combined with modified Transformer layers as a strong configuration, though this does not isolate the loss’s contribution. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that in-batch sampling introduces popularity bias and that correction must account for the positive being included deterministically. These results motivate comparing multi-negative gBCE and sampled softmax before adding adaptive mining.

Hardness requires safeguards. [NARec (2025)](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/aie2.70004) selects challenging sequence-level contrastive negatives from in-batch and global pools; this differs from next-item ranking negatives. [Enhanced BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) explicitly addresses false negatives in hard-negative recommendation training. [SID4SRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705126010221) filters semantically overlapping negatives, but its category/brand features exceed this task’s available inputs. Practical inference: score a modest sampled item pool with batched matrix multiplication, exclude padding, target collisions and observed training positives, then compare uniform sampling against a random/semi-hard mixture. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec encodes interaction sequences with item embeddings, learned positional embeddings, and causal self-attention blocks. Each position predicts the next item through a dot product with shared item embeddings. Attention lets predictions draw on recent actions or longer histories. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
